clue.text: Bringing up a storybook character round about ancient city, getting into trouble

indicators.note: the turned name goes about, i.e. surrounds, the ancient city
turned round, so the character's name is read backwards

parts.note: Tigger is the bouncy tiger in the Winnie-the-Pooh stories
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city of the Chaldees

indicators.note: to trouble is to stir up, so the little words a and into are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone recounts how a storybook figure circled an ancient city and got into a scrape.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'a' is not part of the character: it waits to be rearranged with 'into', the 'trouble' sitting just after them.
explanation.definitionFit: Regurgitation is the act of throwing food back up, so it is a noun matching the gerund phrase.

clue.text: Utter cry of delight about lots of Cajun cooking

indicators.note: the delight word goes about, i.e. around, the cooked letters

parts.note: to delight someone is to elate them

indicators.note: cooking suggests ingredients being mixed up, so the letters are rearranged
lots of a word but not all, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: the word written in the clue, minus its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone whoops with pleasure at a big plate of Louisiana food.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is two words, 'Utter cry', a verb meaning to exclaim; 'of' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To ejaculate, in its older sense, is to exclaim suddenly, to blurt out a short exclamation.

clue.text: Bend, hang and invert

parts.note: a U-bend, the U-shaped trap under a sink, gives the letter U
to pend is an old word for to hang or be suspended

explanation.surface: Instructions for a contortionist: bend over, dangle and turn upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: To upend something is to turn it upside down, which is to invert it.

clue.text: It's sweet of Republicans to keep banging drum

indicators.note: the party letters keep, or hold, the rearranged drum inside them

parts.note: GOP, the Grand Old Party, is the US Republican Party

indicators.note: banging a drum knocks it about, so its letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A sarcastic remark that it is kind of the Republicans to keep up their drumbeat.
explanation.definitionFit: A gumdrop is a chewy jelly confectionery, a kind of sweet or candy.

clue.text: Drunk carrying on with Bernstein number

indicators.note: the drunk word carries the little word inside it

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tipsy fan keeps going while belting out something from Bernstein.
explanation.definitionFit: A song from West Side Story, the musical scored by Leonard Bernstein, is one of his numbers.

clue.text: Dynamic corrosion infecting object

indicators.note: the corrosion gets into the object like an infection

parts.note: an object is a thing
rust is the corrosion of iron

explanation.surface: A sentence about rust spreading through a piece of metal, with an odd opening adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrusting person is pushy and go-getting, which is what dynamic means here.

clue.text: Piscivore and outrageous queen

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means outrageous
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Two characters introduced together: a fish-eater and a flamboyant queen.
explanation.definitionFit: The otter feeds mainly on fish, so it is a fish-eating animal.

clue.text: Raised squadron leader, concerned with Children In Need, to adopt Mr Nazi's bully-boys?

indicators.note: in a down clue raising the letters means reading them from the bottom up
a leader is the first, so the opening letter of squadron

parts.note: re means concerning or about

indicators.note: the children's phrase takes in, as if adopting, the title

parts.note: poor tots are needy children, and Children in Need is a BBC charity appeal
taken as written

explanation.surface: An RAF officer involved with a charity appeal is asked to take in a man, oddly linked to Nazi thugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' reverses S + RE + POORT-MR-OTS (MR 'adopted' into POOR TOTS), giving SREPOORTMROTS read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Stormtroopers were the SA, the Nazi party's paramilitary thugs, so they were its bully-boys.

clue.text: One singer left in county; another on drug amid unknowns

indicators.note: the left letter goes in the county word

parts.note: a shire is a county

indicators.note: the singer and drug sit amid, between, the two unknowns

parts.note: Y is an algebraic unknown, so two unknowns give two Ys
another singer: a bass
E is short for ecstasy

explanation.surface: A list of performers: one from the shires, another a drug-taker surrounded by mystery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' borrows the definition's word: another singer, here BASS, placed on E and between Y and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Shirley Bassey is the Welsh vocalist famous for Bond themes like Goldfinger.

clue.text: Back door user to handle arrow, holding spearhead back

indicators.note: back means the whole assembly is read in reverse
the name word holds the spear's first letter inside it

parts.note: a handle is a name, as in a nickname
the head of spear is its first letter, S
a dart is a small arrow

explanation.surface: Instructions to wield an arrow while keeping the point pulled back.
explanation.walkthrough: NAME 'holding' S gives NAMSE; with DART that is NAMSEDART, which 'back' reverses. A tradesman traditionally calls at the tradesmen's entrance, the back door of a big house.
explanation.definitionFit: Tradesmen delivering goods once had to use the rear entrance of a grand house rather than the front.

clue.text: Pathetic character wanting women to heave

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the women's letter is removed

parts.note: a wretch is a pitiful person

explanation.surface: A sad figure who lacks female company feels like being sick.
explanation.definitionFit: To retch is to heave, making the motions of vomiting without bringing anything up.

clue.text: Such figures end in such a figure

definitions.text: Such figures end in such a figure

parts.words: Such figures end in such a figure
parts.note: numbers like 100 or 2000 are this kind of figure, and they end in a zero, which is itself this shape

explanation.surface: A riddling statement about numbers that end in a certain shape.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'figures' are numbers; the second 'figure' is a shape, the circle of a nought.
explanation.definitionFit: Round numbers end in zeros, and a zero drawn on paper is a circular shape.

clue.text: Recorder thrust right into bum

indicators.note: the thrust and right go into the bum

parts.note: bum is British slang for backside, the rear
the thrust of an argument is its gist

explanation.surface: A crude jab: something rammed into someone's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrust' is a noun, the main point, not a shove.
explanation.definitionFit: A registrar records births, marriages and deaths, so is an official recorder.

clue.text: Drinking place where bard reflected about tree

indicators.note: the turned poet goes about, i.e. around, the tree
seen reflected, as in a mirror, so the poet word is written backwards

parts.note: a bard is a poet
the ash is a tree

explanation.surface: A tavern where a poet looked thoughtfully at a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' turns POET to TEOP, which goes 'about' ASH.
explanation.definitionFit: A teashop is a cafe serving tea, so a place for drinking.

clue.text: Favourite 20 once involving a death? RIP

indicators.note: involving here means entangling or twisting together, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the letters of the gravestone abbreviation

explanation.surface: A gloomy question about whether some old chart hit was about someone dying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' rearranges A DEATH RIP; RIP looks like an epitaph but is just three letters of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The hit parade was the old weekly chart of the most popular records, such as the top twenty.

clue.text: Roundhead boarding weary compiler's boat

indicators.note: the letter boards, or gets on, the weary word

parts.note: to weary is to tire
the head of round is its first letter
the compiler of a crossword refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A Cromwellian soldier climbs aboard the exhausted setter's vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roundhead' looks like a Civil War Parliamentarian but means the first letter of round.
explanation.definitionFit: A trireme was an ancient galley with three banks of oars, a kind of boat.

clue.text: Screwed-up hero getting award from Little Englander?

indicators.note: screwed up means crumpled, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, part of the jumble
taken as written
the OBE, Officer of the Order of the British Empire, is an honour

explanation.surface: A neurotic hero receives a medal from an insular patriot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screwed-up' looks like a description of the hero, but UP is part of the jumble with HERO.
explanation.definitionFit: A Little Englander is an insular Briton, typically hostile to Europe, as a Europhobe is.

clue.text: Undistinguished home secured by blade

indicators.note: the home is held fast between the blade's letters

parts.note: an oar's flat end is its blade, so the blade stands for an oar
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: A house kept safe by a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blade' suggests a knife, but it stands for an OAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-star rating marks the lowest grade, so something one-star is mediocre and unremarkable.

clue.text: Old party spot on time in former capital

indicators.note: the spot and time go in the old capital

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro was Brazil's capital until Brasilia replaced it
a dot is a spot

explanation.surface: A guide naming the right place and moment in an old capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridotto was an eighteenth-century social gathering with music and dancing, a masked ball.

clue.text: Heroin embargo almost ruined part of Africa

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: H is slang for heroin

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: taken as written, then trimmed

explanation.surface: A drugs ban that failed in an African region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims EMBARGO to EMBARG; with H, 'ruined' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maghreb is northwest Africa: Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia and neighbours.

clue.text: Documents about crazy Dane — or his problem?

indicators.note: the documents go about, around, the jumbled letters

parts.note: MSS is short for manuscripts

indicators.note: crazy suggests letters going wild, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Papers about a mad Dane: or was that his trouble?
explanation.walkthrough: The Dane is Hamlet, whose feigned or real insanity is the play's question.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet, the Prince of Denmark, has a problem of apparent insanity, so this names his affliction.

clue.text: Fat European straddling Germany, having lost crown

indicators.note: the European's letters straddle the fat, one part either side

parts.note: a Pole is a European
lard is pig fat
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: An overweight European astride the border of Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: A pollarded tree has had its top branches cut back, losing its head or crown.

clue.text: Name written in the water — French or Austrian poet?

indicators.note: the name is written inside the French words

parts.note: l'eau is French for the water

explanation.surface: A Keatsian echo: a name writ in water, by a French or Austrian poet.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes Keats's epitaph 'Here lies one whose name was writ in water'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikolaus Lenau was a nineteenth-century Austrian Romantic lyric writer.

clue.text: Max maintains love is a recurring theme

indicators.note: maintains means holds, so the love letter sits inside

parts.note: tops means at the maximum, as in 'ten pounds max'
love is zero in tennis, so the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone named Max insists that love keeps coming up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Max' looks like a name but means at most.
explanation.definitionFit: A topos is a traditional motif in literature or rhetoric, a stock theme used over and over.

clue.text: Article on origins of troubled adolescent character

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: the origins are the first letters of the two following words

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about the background of a troubled teenager.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, a character in writing.

clue.text: Welsh valley spoken of in Spanish city

indicators.note: spoken means the valley's name is said aloud

parts.note: the Rhondda is a former coal-mining valley in South Wales

explanation.surface: A Welsh valley mentioned in connection with a city in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Ronda is a hilltop town in Andalusia, famous for its gorge-spanning bridge.

clue.text: So 10 almost bypasses most of county town

indicators.note: a bypass goes round a town, so the trimmed ten goes round the trimmed county town
almost all of it, so its last letter goes

parts.note: the number ten, spelt out

indicators.note: most of the name, dropping its last letter

parts.note: Hereford is the county town, the administrative centre, of Herefordshire

explanation.surface: A traffic report: the road numbered 10 nearly skirts a market town.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' looks like a cross-reference to 10 across but is just the number TEN, cut to TE.
explanation.definitionFit: Therefore and so both introduce a consequence, meaning for that reason.

clue.text: ENO FAQs peed us off at one of their productions?

indicators.note: peed off means annoyed; here off signals the letters being knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Frequently asked questions from English National Opera irritated us at one of their shows.
explanation.walkthrough: ENO is English National Opera, which stages Tchaikovsky's opera of this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Queen of Spades is Tchaikovsky's opera after Pushkin, the kind of work English National Opera stages.
